style_when: the story is a single number, rule, gate or shift and restraint is the point — with no scene to photograph, the frame must still be a real assembly: a modular bay, an unlatched inspection gate, a rack of blades, an interlocking connector
prompt: Minimalist composition of a four-quadrant modular sorting tray assembly resting on a weathered concrete plant floor, extreme asymmetry with generous negative space. The tray is constructed from brushed galvanised steel, divided into a precise grid. One quadrant holds uniform steel blocks, while the others contain scattered, lumpy irregular components. One directional light from the left throwing a long cast shadow. Matte muted palette of graphite, safety yellow, and steel blue. Hard clean edges, no text, no lettering.
negative_prompt: text, garbled letters, numbers, watermarks, humans, people, abstract shapes
rationale: Component assembly perfectly captures the rigid, structural nature of a four-quadrant classification grid without resorting to literal charts. It translates a systemic sorting rule into a tangible mechanical object.
subject: a four-quadrant modular sorting tray with irregular metal parts
core_thesis: Score every SKU on its average demand interval and squared coefficient of variation to identify lumpy items that require buffer stock rather than forecast accuracy.
core_conflict: Mathematical forecasting models vs real-world lumpy demand that breaks statistical predictability.
composition: extreme asymmetry with generous negative space
